content.title: About
content.content: Baby Toddler fruit is a smooth puree made from selected fruits, specially formulated for children aged 6 months to 3 years. The product contains no added sugar, gluten, or artificial flavors, making it a safe and nutritious choice for little ones.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The puree is made from 100 % natural fruits without any concentrates.
It contains apple, pear, banana and peach – fruits rich in vitamins C and A.
The product meets strict NFS (National Food Safety) quality standards.
Packaging is BPA‑free and microwave‑safe.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: The fruit blend provides vitamin C for immune support and vitamin A for healthy vision.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber aids normal digestion and promotes a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: Absence of added sugar helps avoid rapid blood glucose spikes.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The smooth texture is suitable for developing chewing skills in toddlers.

items.title: Supports growth
items.content: Natural fruit sugars and minerals such as potassium and magnesium support overall development.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Children with known fruit allergies should be consulted with a pediatrician before use.

items.title: Storage after opening
items.content: Once opened, keep the package refrigerated and use within 3‑5 days.

items.title: Not suitable for infants under 6 months
items.content: Babies younger than 6 months should receive only breast milk or specially formulated infant formula.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The puree can be served straight from the pouch, mixed into oatmeal, yogurt, or a baby dish. If desired, gently warm in the microwave (no more than 30 seconds), stir and check temperature before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened packages in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated in an airtight container.

content.title: About
content.content: Bread with oatmeal is a whole‑grain loaf that incorporates whole rolled oats into the dough. It has a soft yet slightly dense crumb, a fresh‑baked aroma, and a subtle nutty note from the oats. The product is commonly enjoyed as a hearty breakfast or snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oat flakes increase the fiber content of the bread, making it more filling.
Traditional oatmeal bread recipes originated in Scandinavian countries in the 19th century.
Oats contain beta‑glucans, which help lower cholesterol levels.
Oat bread is often used in weight‑control diets because of its relatively low glycemic index.
When baked, oat flakes create a crunchy crust if sprinkled on top before baking.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Whole oats and whole‑grain flour provide both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains beta‑glucans
items.content: Beta‑glucans help reduce LDL cholesterol and stabilize blood glucose levels.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The loaf supplies thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: It contains iron, magnesium, and zinc, important for blood formation and immune function.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of carbs and protein slows digestion, helping to control appetite.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The bread contains wheat, so it is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic impact if sweetened
items.content: When sugar or honey is added to the recipe, the product can raise blood sugar levels.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Oats contain phytic acid, which may reduce the absorption of certain minerals if consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Oat bread can be eaten plain, topped with cottage cheese, avocado, or used for sandwiches. It pairs well with honey, jam, and works nicely as a base for croutons.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the loaf in a paper bag or bread box at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in an airtight bag for up to 2 months. Thaw at room temperature before use.

content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate puffs are dry corn flakes coated with a sweet chocolate glaze. They have a crunchy texture and a pronounced chocolate flavor, making them a popular breakfast cereal and snack for both children and adults.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial chocolate puff cereal appeared in the 1970s.
The flakes are toasted under high pressure to achieve their crispness.
The chocolate coating is typically made from cocoa butter, sugar, and milk powder.
In many markets the product is fortified with vitamins and minerals.
Packaging often uses bright colors to attract children’s attention.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates provide a quick source of energy, convenient for an active start to the day.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Fortified versions often include iron, which is essential for blood formation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B6 support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Added calcium helps strengthen bones and teeth.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: A modest amount of fiber aids digestion.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Added sugars can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The formula may contain milk, soy, or nuts, which are important to note for people with food allergies.

items.title: Glycemic index
items.content: The cereal has a high glycemic index, which can cause rapid spikes in blood glucose.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Some varieties contain artificial flavors and preservatives that may cause sensitivity in certain individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chocolate puffs are typically served with milk or yogurt. They can be added to smoothies, used as a topping for desserts, or eaten dry as a snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cereal in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the bag tightly closed to prevent moisture absorption.

chicken-and-vegetables-au-gratin-with-ri.title: Chicken and vegetables au gratin with rice, diet frozen entree

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken and vegetables au gratin with rice is a diet frozen entree designed for quick and convenient preparation. It contains tender chicken breast, a mix of carrots, broccoli and cauliflower, topped with a light cheese crust, and served with steamed rice.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is produced by a company with over 30 years of experience in frozen foods.
The cheese crust is made from reduced‑fat cheese, lowering calories without sacrificing flavor.
The rice used is whole‑grain, providing longer lasting satiety.
Each serving provides approximately 250 kcal, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.
The product has been tested for flavor and texture retention after freezing and microwave reheating.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken supplies high‑quality protein essential for maintaining muscle mass.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Reduced‑fat cheese and chicken breast keep the dish low in fat, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vegetables and chicken provide vitamins B6 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: Vegetables and whole‑grain rice add dietary fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The meal contains potassium, magnesium and iron, important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The cheese crust may trigger reactions in individuals allergic to milk proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: People monitoring salt intake should note the moderate sodium level in the dish.

items.title: Heating requirements
items.content: Improper reheating can lead to uneven heating and loss of flavor.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Microwave the frozen entree on high for 3–4 minutes, or bake in a preheated oven at 180 °C for 12–15 minutes until the crust turns golden. Stir before serving to evenly distribute the sauce and rice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen product at –18 °C or lower. Once the package is opened, use within 24 hours if the product has been thawed.

content.title: About
content.content: Fish with tomato-based sauce is a ready‑to‑eat dish featuring poached or baked white fish (commonly cod, haddock or sea bass) covered in a flavorful sauce made from tomatoes, onion, garlic and herbs. The meal is rich in high‑quality protein, omega‑3 fatty acids and B‑vitamins, while the tomato sauce adds lycopene and vitamin C.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The sauce traditionally includes basil or oregano, which enhances its aroma.
Fish in tomato sauce is a staple of Mediterranean cuisine, especially in Italy and Spain.
Lycopene retains most of its antioxidant power even after cooking.
The dish is often served with rice, pasta or mashed potatoes as a side.
Tomatoes in the sauce can be fresh or canned, making preparation convenient.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Fish provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: EPA and DHA support heart health and brain function.

items.title: Vitamin C and lycopene
items.content: The tomato sauce supplies vitamin C and the powerful antioxidant lycopene, which help protect cells.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Fish contains B12, niacin and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish provides selenium, iodine and phosphorus, supporting thyroid function and bone health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauces often contain added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt versions.

items.title: Potential toxins
items.content: Certain fish species can accumulate mercury; it is advisable to use small‑size fish from reputable sources.

items.title: Acidity of tomatoes
items.content: Tomatoes may increase stomach acidity, which can be problematic for gastritis or heartburn sufferers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The dish is ready to eat after reheating. Serve hot with boiled rice, couscous, pasta or a fresh vegetable salad. Optionally garnish with chopped herbs, a squeeze of lemon or a drizzle of olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C in an airtight container for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C; when thawed, reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C.

content.title: About
content.content: Pork with chili and tomatoes is a dish where tender pieces of pork are simmered with hot chili peppers and ripe tomatoes. The combination of meat, the spicy kick of chili, and the sweet‑tart flavor of tomatoes creates a rich, aromatic sauce suitable for lunch or dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Chili peppers contain capsaicin, which gives the heat and can boost metabolism.
Pork provides high‑quality protein, vitamin B12, and zinc.
The dish is popular in Latin American and Asian cuisines, often enhanced with fresh herbs and spices.
Tomatoes and chili together improve iron absorption from the meat.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Pork supplies complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C from tomatoes and vitamin B12 from pork help maintain a healthy immune system.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene in tomatoes and capsaicin in chili help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Improved digestion
items.content: Capsaicin stimulates gastric secretions, aiding digestion.

items.title: Heart‑healthy fats
items.content: Lean cuts of pork contain monounsaturated fats that can support healthy cholesterol levels.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Adding soy sauce or extra salt can make the dish high in sodium, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Chili heat
items.content: Too much chili may irritate the stomach of people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Pork must be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 71 °C to eliminate salmonella and trichinella.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or tomato juice.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sear pork pieces until golden, then add diced onion, garlic, and chili. Simmer with tomato puree, broth, and spices for 20‑30 minutes until the meat is tender. Serve over rice, quinoa, or garnish with fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. It can be frozen for up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge before reheating.

content.title: About
content.content: Soft pretzels filled with cheese are a baked snack made from yeasted dough, brushed with a golden crust and stuffed with melted cheese. They have a tender flavor, a slightly salty aroma, and a gooey cheese center.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cheese‑filled soft pretzels are a popular bar and café snack in the United States.
The traditional German "Brezel" has a hard crust; the soft version emerged in the early 20th century in the US.
Cheese fillings often include cheddar, mozzarella, or a blend of several cheeses.
In some regions they are served with mustard or honey dipping sauces.
Spiced versions add paprika, garlic, or other seasonings to the dough.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: The cheese filling provides both dairy and plant protein, supporting tissue repair.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Cheese contributes calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast‑leavened dough is rich in B1, B2, and B6 vitamins, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: Soft pretzels deliver fast‑acting carbohydrates for an energy boost.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: When whole‑grain flour is used, the pretzel contains more fiber, beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: The cheese filling can trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or dairy protein allergy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Salt used in the dough and filling may be a concern for those monitoring sodium intake.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Cheese‑filled soft pretzels are relatively calorie‑dense, so they should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The dough contains wheat, making the product unsuitable for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pretzels can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, sliced and paired with mustard, cheese sauce, or a tomato dip. They also work well as a base for mini sandwiches or appetizer bites.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store soft pretzels in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer shelf life keep them refrigerated – up to a week – or freeze and reheat in the oven before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Ramen bowl with fish is a ready‑to‑cook kit that includes wheat ramen noodles, a flavorful fish broth, dried pieces of salmon or other fish, and a blend of seasonings and vegetable additives. It is designed for quick preparation while delivering a traditional ramen experience.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ramen originated in Japan but now has countless regional variations worldwide.
Fish broth is often made from fish bones and heads, giving it a deep umami flavor.
Dried fish pieces retain most of their nutrients thanks to low‑temperature dehydration.
Traditional Japanese ramen is commonly garnished with sliced green onion, nori, and a soft‑boiled egg.
Instant ramen kits can be prepared in 3‑5 minutes, preserving much of the authentic taste.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: The fish pieces provide omega‑3 fatty acids that support heart and vascular health.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: A serving delivers about 15‑20 g of high‑quality protein for tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Ramen with fish contains vitamin B12 and niacin, important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies iodine, selenium, and iron, which aid thyroid function and immune health.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Warm broth stimulates gastric secretions, helping digestion.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: People allergic to seafood should avoid this product as it may trigger reactions.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The broth can be salty; individuals with hypertension should limit portion size.

items.title: Monosodium glutamate (MSG)
items.content: Some kits contain MSG, which can cause sensitivity in certain individuals.

items.title: Gluten presence
items.content: Ramen noodles are wheat‑based, making the product unsuitable for gluten‑free diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour boiling water (about 95 °C) over the contents, cover, and let sit for 3‑4 minutes. Add fresh vegetables, herbs, or a soft‑boiled egg to taste. Optionally enhance with soy sauce or chili oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened package in a cool, dry place away from moisture. After opening, consume within 1‑2 days and reseal tightly.

rice-white-with-carrots-and-dark-green-v.title: White Rice with Carrots and Dark Green Vegetables, Fat Added

content.title: About
content.content: A ready‑to‑eat dish made from boiled white rice, carrots and dark green vegetables (such as broccoli or spinach), prepared with a small amount of added vegetable fat. It has a mild flavor, a hint of sweetness from the carrots, and the fresh taste of the greens.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The combination of white rice and carrots is a staple in many Asian and Eastern European cuisines.
Dark green vegetables are rich in chlorophyll, giving them their vivid color and distinctive flavor.
Adding a little fat improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins from the vegetables.
The dish is often served in school cafeterias as a source of energy and vitamins for children.
When stored properly, it stays fresh for up to 3 days in the refrigerator.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice provides quick‑digesting carbohydrates, while the added fat raises the calorie content, useful for active individuals.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both rice and carrots contain B1, B3 and B6 vitamins that support metabolism.

items.title: Beta‑carotene
items.content: Carrots are high in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A for eye health.

items.title: Antioxidants from greens
items.content: Dark green vegetables supply lutein and zeaxanthin, protecting the eyes from oxidative stress.

items.title: Fat‑soluble vitamins
items.content: The added vegetable fat helps the body absorb vitamins A, D, E and K found in the greens.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Because of the added fat, the dish can be calorie‑dense, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Allergy to vegetable oils
items.content: Some individuals may react to the type of oil used (e.g., sunflower or olive oil).

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: If seasoned with salt, sodium intake should be monitored, especially for people with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a standalone meal or as a side dish with meat, fish, or tofu. It reheats well in the microwave or on the stovetop; add a splash of water to prevent drying out.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 2 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Seabreeze is a light non‑alcoholic beverage with a sea‑breeze flavor, made from natural citrus extracts, sea salt, and gentle carbonation. It refreshes, contains no sugar, and is suitable for all ages.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The recipe uses sea salt harvested from pristine oceanic sources.
Flavor is created by a blend of lime, grapefruit and a hint of mint.
Seabreeze was first launched at the International Healthy Food Expo in 2022.
The drink contains no artificial sweeteners or colorings.
With low calories (15 kcal/100 ml) it is popular among athletes.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Gentle carbonation and electrolytes from sea salt help maintain the body’s water balance.

items.title: Low Calorie Content
items.content: Ideal for those watching their calorie intake while still enjoying flavor.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Citrus extracts provide a modest amount of vitamin C, supporting immunity.

items.title: Antioxidant Effect
items.content: Flavonoids from grapefruit have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Refreshing Sensation
items.content: Mint and lime create a fresh feeling that reduces thirst.

items.title: Citrus Allergy
items.content: People allergic to citrus may experience a reaction.

items.title: Sodium Content
items.content: Although the amount of salt is small, individuals with hypertension should consider total sodium intake.

items.title: Carbonation
items.content: Carbonated drinks can cause stomach discomfort in some individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Seabreeze chilled; optionally add a lime wedge or a sprig of mint. It works as a standalone drink, in non‑alcoholic cocktails, or as a refreshing accompaniment to light meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days.
